entries.justification: Pre-existing local aspect-strength dict; B-02 stream will migrate to brahmagyan.aspects oracle. Line updated 231→302 (2026-10-02, S-L1 integration branch: the merged lanes #2854/#2941/#2893/#2960 add 71 lines above the unchanged dict; verified by check_no_local_aspect_dict.py); 230→231 (2026-10-02, TI-l1-writer-fixes-001: one import line added above); earlier 224→230 (2026-09-29, l3/gochara-autonomous-wp0-7): branch insertions above (_citation_human_strength G-10 clause, +6 lines) shifted the unchanged, byte-identical dict; verified against origin/main:224-232.

SPECIAL_DRISHTI_DEG is the DELIBERATE pinned doctrine for the new gochara kernel, not an oracle bypass: WP1_CONTRACTS.md §7 + §2.2 N-14 (RULED) — Rāhu/Ketu cast NO dṛṣṭi (empty angle set), superseding the served nodal entries (F-29). brahmagyan.aspects.get_graha_aspects() carries the OPPOSITE nodal convention ('Rahu/Ketu cast the same special aspects as Jupiter', aspects.py:26), so importing it would violate the N-14 ruling. B-02 migration would require an oracle-side doctrinal change first; out of this lane's scope.

DELIBERATE independent restatement, not an oracle bypass: the gochara verifier re-derives the builder's output from the spec text and imports nothing from the builder (ND-ROLES option A; independent re-derivation is the point of a separate verifier — importing the shared oracle would make the check agree with the builder by construction). Same pinned doctrine as services/gochara_kernel/convention.py (WP1_CONTRACTS.md §7 + §2.2 N-14: Rahu/Ketu cast NO drishti, the opposite of brahmagyan.aspects' nodal convention). A test asserts the verifier's table equals the kernel's. Added 2026-10-03, PR #2999 CI (D-01a), Pravaha A5.3.
